text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet presented measures for speeding up structural reforms to heads of parliamentary committees and regional governors at a closed door session last night.
Steps for overcoming the acute wheat shortage, new bank closures, speeding up privatisaton in metallurgy, chemical and pharmaceutical industry and military industry were on the agenda. @

-- U.S. investment banks Merrill Lynch and J.P. Morgan have demanded an additional weekly interest of 20 percent on Bulgaria's one-month treasury bills they have bought to compensate them for losses due to the sharp lev's fall against the dollar on the domestic forex market.

-- International auditors Deloitte & Touche that won a tender for auditing of Bulgaria's central bank (BNB) will sign the auditing contract with the BNB today and is expected to announce the results by October 31. @
-- The World Bank's representative for Europe Kenneth Lay arrives in Sofia today to meet bank's local representatives, the bank's press office said.
Lay will have talks with Bulgarian National Bank board of governors to discuss its monetary policy, central bank officials said.

-- Bulgarian citizens' income is expected to fall by 25-30 percent on the average this year, said Ivan Angelov, a former economic advisor to Prime Minister Zhan Videnov, told a private radio station. @

Angelov also said a second revision of the state budget is inevitable by the end of the year to adjust for the fall in production, the quickening inflation and the sharp fall of the lev against the dollar.
-- The Sofia City Court is expected on Wednesday to begin hearings on an bankruptcy case against First Private Bank requested by the central bank in May.

-- Bulgarian citizens' deposits in local banks may not be 100 percent guaranteed by the state in case of future bank bankruptcies, a socialist party deputy said before the closed door cabinet meeting last night.

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it has approved the sale of up to 60 percent stake in the Devnya-based chemical giant Sodi, which will be completed after negotiations with potential buyers. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
